title: Building with live XAUUSD and forex market data?
author: Delicious-Equipment4
selftext:
Hi everyone! 👋

I'm part of the team behind [**TickFeed.pro**](http://TickFeed.pro), a market-data API for developers building trading applications, automated strategies and financial tools.

We provide programmatic access to forex and metals quotes, including XAUUSD (gold), as well as historical market data.

We're looking to connect with developers who are building:

* 🤖 Automated trading bots and algorithmic strategies
* 📊 Gold-price dashboards and market-analysis tools
* 🧪 Backtesting systems using historical candles
* 🧠 AI applications that work with financial market data

If you're working on a project that needs market data, you can explore our API and documentation here:

🌐 [https://tickfeed.pro/](https://tickfeed.pro/)

I'd also be interested to hear from developers about what matters most when choosing a market-data provider: pricing, data freshness, historical coverage or ease of integration.

**Full disclosure:** I'm involved with TickFeed, so this is a company introduction rather than an independent recommendation.

Happy to answer technical questions about the API and its supported features.

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
If I were comparing data providers, I'd want to see what a gold tick looks like and how far back the candles go before I looked at pricing. Putting a short code sample with a real XAUUSD response, the rate limit and the history depth for each timeframe in the post itself would answer most of your own question for readers. Your disclosure line is a good touch; keep it in every post.

comments.author: Individual-Quote-958
comments.body: For XAUUSD, I’d check the timestamp convention and candle boundary first: whether bars are stamped at open or close, and what timezone defines a day. A quick sanity check is to compare a few raw quotes against the candles around the daily rollover, since that’s where gaps and spread changes can get hidden. Then compare history depth and missing intervals for the exact timeframes you plan to backtest.
